brief.recommendation: The root blocker batch_replayable_inventory (pid 1663616) has been idle for only 4.2s with last statement SELECT 1, suggesting imminent completion. Waiting avoids the $199,166 revenue-at-risk from checkout degradation, and terminating would incur a 4-minute replay cost for an idempotent, may_interrupt batch workload. biz.change_calendar (BIZ-5) confirms no active window covers this workload, and db.protected_settlements (DB-2) confirms no protected settlements are in flight. These invariants are satisfied, making wait the lower-risk choice given the short elapsed time and idempotent replay availability.

audit.report: The checkout system degraded after a batch inventory reconciliation process (batch_replayable_inventory) acquired a lock on the database and entered an idle-in-transaction state. The root blocker (pid 1663616) had been waiting 4.2 seconds with a SELECT 1 statement. The database guardian recommended waiting, but the continuity guardian rejected all proposals because waiting ~896 seconds would exceed the 60-second business tolerance for checkout degradation (costing ~$199,166 in lost revenue), while terminating would only require a 4-minute, idempotent replay of the inventory reconciliation job. The negotiation escalated to inventory-platform with no resolution within three rounds.
audit.root_cause: A batch inventory reconciliation job (batch_replayable_inventory) became the root blocker, holding a lock while idle in transaction, which degraded checkout success rates from 55% to 28% and put approximately $199,166/min of revenue at risk.
lessons: Terminate idle-in-transaction batch workers immediately when checkout SLOs are breaching; the 4-minute replay cost for inventory_reconcile is acceptable compared to the $199,166/min revenue loss from prolonged checkout degradation.

Pre-negotiate interruptibility policies for batch jobs that share critical paths with checkout; inventory_reconcile already has may_interrupt and idempotent semantics, but this was not checked before the 60-second degradation window was exceeded.
audit.negotiation_critique: The database guardian consistently proposed waiting based on the short 4.2s idle time, while the continuity guardian correctly invoked invariant I7 to reject waits exceeding 60s, but the exchange wasted three rounds because the required calendar and protected-settlement evidence was not probed until after the trade-off analysis was complete.
follow_ups: Add a pre-negotiation checklist that runs biz.workload_registry, biz.change_calendar, and db.protected_settlements probes before any wait/terminate proposal is generated.
Configure the system to auto-terminate any root blocker idle >5s when checkout success falls below 90%, bypassing the full trade-off calculation to preserve revenue.
Escalate the inventory_reconcile job ownership to inventory-platform with a request to either reschedule during low-traffic windows or provide a non-interruptible variant for audit compliance.
